metadata.title: A Dark Sector the MOND Kernel Cannot See: Reciprocity, Bound-Region Kernels, and the Cosmic-Shear Pincer
metadata.description:
The programme's previous two notes (PAPER32, PAPER33) found that two relativistic completions of a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) fail as built, and left a specification: the cosmic web and the z ~ 2-3 intergalactic medium must stay Newtonian, the Mpc-scale lensing around isolated galaxies must be supplied, whatever supplies it must not be MOND-boosted, and the MOND kernel must not read the large-scale field. This note reports the constructions built to that specification and the gates they were put through. Every number comes from a committed script, run on both a0 footings wherever a0 enters unless stated, and an audit lane re-derives the 244 numbers the note quotes from the committed outputs.

Reciprocity. If each species couples linearly to the fields of a static Lagrangian, the species-response matrix is symmetric. A dark component the kernel cannot see therefore feels Newtonian gravity only; a dark component that feels the baryons' MOND field while its own field stays unboosted has no action (it breaks momentum balance by a factor nu ~ r/r_M).

A kernel-invisible dark component exists as a Lagrangian construction (a subtraction pair of auxiliary fields). It leaves the baryons' boost, tracking and modes unchanged and predicts a dark-sector equivalence-principle violation: at R500 in X-COP clusters the dark component feels 47% (37-53%) less acceleration than the gas.

Blindness to dark matter is not enough. A kernel that reads all baryons still feels the web's baryonic field, about 30 times what KiDS-1000 isolated lensing allows. Two kernels blind to the large-scale field are built from actions: a region-local QUMOND screened across the inactive web, whose switch is gated by the vacuum's share of the expansion (this opens the KiDS-forest pincer of any constant threshold); and a generated phantom whose source, not its flux, is switched.

Cosmic shear. Galaxy-galaxy lensing, a cross-correlation, constrains only the sum of the mass private to each lens and the mass shared with its neighbours; cosmic shear separates them. For both kernels, the private phantom KiDS wants, added to a LCDM-like dark field, raises the lensing power at k = 0.3-1 h/Mpc by factors of 1.5-9.

Replacement. If the dark component converts, at a rate set by Omega_Lambda(z), into a hot state that free-streams, the phantom can stand in for its small-scale power. The generated phantom (1 Mpc screening) plus such a component passes KiDS (the record's acceptance), cosmic shear, X-COP, the galaxies' radial acceleration relation, S8 and the Lyman-alpha forest together on the alternative threshold set. On the strict set only the forest blocks it (4.3-4.7 keV thermal-relic equivalent, against 5.3 keV), once the strict S8 floor is corrected to KiDS-Legacy's lower error bar (0.752, not 0.767). The window sits at one screening length, and KiDS prefers longer screening than cosmic shear allows: the window cells score Delta chi^2 = +19 to +21 against the best realisable lens tested (this corrects the repository's earlier 'about +8').

The price is at high redshift. The components built here are intact at z ~ 2.5, as the forest requires, and shift the deep-MOND Tully-Fisher zero point by +0.8 to +1.0 dex (LCDM-calibrated halo masses) against 0.00 for the framework alone: the dark sector and the flagship flat-a0(z) test pull against each other. The dark component is read as a state of the framework's own field, not a new particle; that reading keeps the mass, which clusters and the CMB require, and does not yet supply the hot, multistreaming state the window needs. kappa is not touched and remains fitted. AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed; nothing is claimed closed.
